About

Background & Expertise

Civil engineer with 12 years of continuous site and management experience on the 1,020 MW Punatsangchhu-II Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan — one of South Asia's largest underground powerhouse complexes. Progressed from Graduate Engineer through Site Engineer to Project Engineer and Divisional Head across a single, long-form infrastructure programme.

Specialist in reinforced concrete construction supervision, underground cavern works, contract administration, cost control, and quality management (ITPs/ITCs) across a project comprising the Machine Hall cavern (240.7m×23.5m×51m), 20+ km of tunnels, 3 pressure shafts, and 6 penstocks.

Holds a Master of Professional Engineering (Civil & Construction, Distinction) from Queensland University of Technology (GPA 6.125/7.0) and a Positive Skills Assessment by Engineers Australia (ANZSCO 233211). Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485) — full work rights until 27 February 2027.

Experience

Career Timeline

Twelve consecutive years on a single, major infrastructure programme — the 1,020 MW Punatsangchhu-II Hydroelectric Project, Bhutan.

Project Engineer
1,020 MW Civil Infrastructure Project — Bhutan · Government-Owned Project Authority
Jul 2021 — Jan 2023
  • Divisional Head — managed a team of 7 engineers; assigned tasks, set monthly targets, and oversaw division performance across concurrent civil work packages within the underground powerhouse complex.
  • Oversaw and verified contractor claims across AUD 197M in contracts (AUD 87.5M executed during tenure); reduced billing disputes by 90% through joint measurement verification.
  • Prepared the complete cost estimate of AUD 147.5M for the civil works package at tender approval, incorporating escalation provisions and contingencies per CWC guidelines (GCC Sub-Clause 52(ii)).
  • Managed civil construction of the underground Machine Hall cavern (240.7m×23.5m×51m) through all six concreting stages for 6 Francis turbine units across a 191m×21.5m RC floor structure.
  • Designed SCC M30A20 mix to resolve a critical constructability challenge — spiral casing pressurised at 28±1 kg/cm² during pour; SCC flowed without vibration, eliminating casing displacement risk across all 6 units.
  • Managed construction of the dual 250MT EOT crane beam system at EL 595 (205.4m rail span, 21,000mm gauge) enabling synchronised 350MT rotor lift.
  • Managed construction of the 7-storey Annexe Bay building (42.7m total height, EL 564–EL 600.5) and 5-storey Auxiliary Bay — both RC-framed structures integrated into the main powerhouse frame.
  • Introduced OK Card System requiring formal stakeholder sign-off before each concreting pour, eliminating ambiguities across all 6 turbine barrel concreting stages.
  • Received formal Audit Clearance Certificate from the Royal Audit Authority of Bhutan — zero unresolved audit findings across 12 consecutive years of annual joint audits.
Site Engineer
1,020 MW Civil Infrastructure Project — Bhutan · Government-Owned Project Authority
Jul 2016 — Jul 2021
  • Supervised excavation and primary support construction of the Machine Hall cavern: 36Ø rock bolts (12,000/10,000mm, tensioned to 12T), 200mm SFRS, ISMB 350 steel ribs; rock classified per Barton's Q system.
  • Managed full restrengthening of the Downstream Surge Gallery cavity (46,692m³) 107m below ground — coordinated muck filling, installed 916×20m FMI rock bolts, crown grouting, and progressive demucking; cavity captured via CMS V500 laser scan.
  • Monitored all geotechnical instrumentation: Multi-Point Borehole Extensometers (MPBXs), Instrumented Rock Bolts (IRBs), load cells, and pore pressure gauges throughout excavation and construction phases.
  • Supervised all six sequential structural concrete stages per equipment bay: draft tube liner encasement, pit liner, SCC spiral casing pour (M30A20), stay ring, stator pedestal, and generator foundation concreting.
  • Constructed machine hall drainage, dewatering and flood protection sump system — three RC sumps founded at EL 550.70 (13.3m below FFL EL 564); total plan footprint 23,900×16,375mm.
  • Secured management approval for benching methodology not in original construction plan, enabling concurrent shotcreting, rock bolting, and wall grouting without disrupting excavation progress.
  • Processed monthly billing of AUD 300,000–400,000; prepared BOQs, bar bending schedules, RA Bills, and progress certifications.
Graduate Engineer
1,020 MW Civil Infrastructure Project — Bhutan · Government-Owned Project Authority
Jul 2011 — Jul 2016
  • Led supervision of three major access tunnels totalling 1,404m: Main Access Tunnel (8m×8.5m×906m); ADIT to Tail Race Tunnel (7.5m×7.5m×370m); ADIT to Downstream Surge Gallery (7.5m×7.5m×128m) — including steel rib installation, rock anchoring, 200mm SFRS, and drainage.
  • Coordinated with resident geologist to maintain powder factor below 1 during portal excavation, preserving tunnel profile and minimising overbreak.
  • Maintained and supervised a 5km heavy vehicle access road (Water Bound Macadam) under active construction traffic management.
  • Optimised bar bending schedules to prevent five days of potential project delay; prepared and processed monthly billing of AUD 300,000–400,000.
Projects

Key Projects

Selected highlights from 12 years of professional practice and postgraduate academic study at QUT (2023–2024).

Machine Hall cavern — excavation phase  |  240.7m × 23.5m × 51m

1,020 MW Underground Powerhouse — Machine Hall Construction

Complete vertical construction sequence of the Machine Hall cavern from draft tube liner (EL 555.84) through six RC barrel stages to generator floor (EL 582) and dual 250MT EOT crane beam (EL 595). Designed SCC M30A20 mix to encapsulate pressurised spiral casing (28±1 kg/cm²) without vibration — applied across all 6 Francis turbine units. Divisional Head overseeing AUD 197M in contracts.

RC Barrel Concreting SCC M30A20 Mix Design Underground Cavern EOT Crane Beam AUD 197M 6 × Francis Turbines

DSSG Cavity Restrengthening — 46,692 m³

Managed full restrengthening of the Downstream Surge Gallery cavity following large crown failure 107m below ground. Coordinated muck filling, installed 916×20m FMI rock bolts, crown grouting, and protective sand-packing of completed Machine Hall structures. Cavity surveyed via CMS V500 laser scan.

Geotechnical Rock Bolting Cavity Remediation CMS Laser Scan

Gilmour Highway Upgrade — Geometric Design (8.72 km)

Led geometric design of an 8.72km rural/urban road upgrade per Austroads AGRD guidelines. Designed 4 cross-section types, computed LCS for 5 horizontal curves, redesigned all curves with increased radii and superelevation up to 4%, and designed 3 intersections (priority T, signalised at-grade, roundabout).

Civil 3D Austroads AGRD Geometric Design Drainage Design

Traffic Corridor Analysis — Redbank Plains Road

Developed AIMSUN microsimulation and SIDRA network models for a 7-intersection corridor (Ipswich CBD to Springfield Central). Signal optimisation at 4 junctions delivered +5.56% average network speed and −5.5% delay reduction — with no physical infrastructure changes.

AIMSUN SIDRA Traffic Modelling Signal Optimisation

200 m Earth Dam — Design & Stability Analysis

Designed a zoned earth dam using GeoStudio (SEEP/W & SLOPE/W). Performed core permeability optimisation achieving 33% seepage reduction, slope stability analysis via 5 limit equilibrium methods, and rapid drawdown modelling establishing a 5.011m permissible drawdown limit.

GeoStudio SEEP/W SLOPE/W Geotechnical

Moggill Pocket Bridge — Feasibility Study

Led multidisciplinary team on a full infrastructure feasibility study to replace the Moggill Ferry (est. 1873) across the Brisbane River. Covered geotechnical analysis (slope stability FoS=3.85, pile capacity calculations), environmental impact assessment, Indigenous cultural heritage obligations, and DBYD utility coordination.

Feasibility Study GeoStudio Environmental Stakeholders
